disclosures.name: TestSignalTrace
disclosures.signature: the go2cs managed runtime has no execution tracer
disclosures.reason: the test wraps its signal exercise in runtime/trace.Start, and Go's execution tracer is a serialization of the scheduler the managed host does not have: StartTrace stops the world through the g/m/p machinery (semacquire's first step is getg, a per-thread runtime structure with no CLR counterpart). runtime.StartTrace returns an error by signature, so the linux hand-own answers a named tracing-not-supported error — the AllThreadsSyscall→ENOTSUP fidelity pattern — and the test fails cleanly asserting trace output it cannot have. The signal delivery under the trace is the part this row's siblings already prove; the tracer itself is the same class of unimplementable runtime machinery as WriteHeapDump

disclosures.name: TestTerminalSignal
disclosures.reason: the test needs a real controlling terminal: it opens a pty through the cgo testpty helper (posix_openpt via C), hands the child the slave side with Setctty/Foreground, and drives job control across SIGTTOU. The converted testpty has no cgo and answers its not-supported error, which the test hard-asserts into *testpty.PtyError (the panic this signature pins); behind that sits the controlling-terminal spawn surface (SysProcAttr.Setctty/Foreground) that the posix_spawn seam names as its honest wall — posix_spawn cannot express the tcsetpgrp-between-fork-and-exec dance
